guarantees.claim: All driven outputs default to 0 or inactive values (MuBi4False for absorbed_d) before the unique case, ensuring safe inactive state unless a case branch overrides them.
In StPadIdle, if start_i is asserted, next state is StPrefix when mode_eq_cshake is true, otherwise StMessage; if start_i is not asserted, next state remains StPadIdle.

In StPrefix, sel_mux is set to MuxPrefix; if sent_blocksize is true, next state is StPrefixWait, keccak_run_o = 1, fsm_keccak_valid = 0, clr_sentmsg = 1; otherwise next state stays StPrefix and fsm_keccak_valid = 1.
In StPrefixWait, sel_mux = MuxPrefix; if keccak_complete_i is true, next state is StMessage; otherwise next state remains StPrefixWait.

In StMessage, sel_mux = MuxFifo; when msg_valid_i and msg_partial are true, en_msgbuf = 1 and next state is StMessage; when sent_blocksize, next state is StMessageWait, keccak_run_o = 1, clr_sentmsg = 1, hold_msg = 1; when process_latched or process_i, next state is StPad and hold_msg = 1; otherwise next state stays StMessage.
In StMessageWait, hold_msg = 1; if keccak_complete_i is true, next state is StMessage; otherwise next state remains StMessageWait.

In StPad, sel_mux = MuxFuncPad, fsm_keccak_valid = 1; if keccak_ack and end_of_block are true, next state is StPadRun, clr_msgbuf = 1, clr_sentmsg = 1; else if keccak_ack, next state is StPad01, clr_msgbuf = 1; else next state stays StPad.
In StPadRun, next state is StPadFlush, keccak_run_o = 1, clr_sentmsg = 1.

In StPad01, sel_mux = MuxZeroEnd; if sent_blocksize is true, next state is StPadFlush, fsm_keccak_valid = 0, keccak_run_o = 1, clr_sentmsg = 1; otherwise next state stays StPad01 and fsm_keccak_valid = 1.
In StPadFlush, clr_sentmsg = 1, clr_msgbuf = 1; if keccak_complete_i is true, next state is StPadIdle and absorbed_d = MuBi4True; otherwise next state remains StPadFlush.
In StTerminalError, next state remains StTerminalError and sparse_fsm_error_o = 1, making it a terminal state.
Any state encoding not matching the named states (through default branch) causes next state to become StTerminalError and sparse_fsm_error_o = 1.
When lc_escalate_en_i is true (loose test), st_d is unconditionally forced to StTerminalError, overriding any other state transition and forcing the FSM into terminal error.

assumptions.claim: start_i is a single-cycle pulse that is deasserted before the FSM returns to StPadIdle, preventing immediate re-triggering of a new hash operation.
assumptions.cond: Falling edge of start_i before next Idle
assumptions.risk: A sustained start_i could cause back-to-back starts, unintended repeated hashing, or state machine lockup.

assumptions.claim: mode_eq_cshake is stable and valid at the rising edge of start_i and remains constant throughout the hash operation.
assumptions.risk: If mode changes mid-operation, the FSM may follow an incorrect path, drop prefix, or apply wrong padding, leading to hash corruption.

assumptions.claim: sent_blocksize accurately signals that a complete block of data (prefix or message) has been sent to the keccak round, and it is cleared by clr_sentmsg when no longer applicable.
assumptions.cond: During prefix, message, or pad phases
assumptions.risk: False assertion may prematurely trigger keccak_run_o, lose synchronization, or cause padding on incomplete data, corrupting the hash.

assumptions.claim: keccak_complete_i is deasserted after the FSM acknowledges it, and becomes asserted only after keccak_run_o was previously asserted, forming a valid handshake.
assumptions.cond: When FSM is in StPrefixWait, StMessageWait, or StPadFlush
assumptions.risk: A stuck-high keccak_complete_i would cause the FSM to skip wait states and potentially overflow keccak input or miss completion.

assumptions.claim: keccak_ack and end_of_block are valid combinatorial signals during the cycle following a keccak data accept, and end_of_block correctly indicates the last byte of the current block.
assumptions.cond: In StPad when keccak_ack is true
assumptions.risk: Incorrect end_of_block could cause the FSM to skip StPad01 or mis-handle final block padding, altering the hash result.

assumptions.claim: process_i and process_latched represent a stable request to finalize the message; once asserted they remain high until the FSM moves to StPad.
assumptions.risk: A glitch or deassertion could cause the FSM to miss the finalization and drop data or never enter padding.

assumptions.claim: msg_valid_i and msg_partial correctly indicate the presence of a partial message word; msg_partial is only true when the last word of a message block is incomplete.
assumptions.risk: If msg_partial is asserted for full words, the message buffer could be incorrectly enabled, causing misaligned data and hash corruption.

assumptions.claim: lc_escalate_en_i is a glitch-free, monotonic lifecycle signal that remains asserted after escalation.
assumptions.risk: Glitches on lc_escalate_en_i could trigger a transient error state or cause spurious error outputs.

uncertain_points.claim: In StMessage, when msg_valid_i is true and msg_partial is false (full word), the FSM does not assert en_msgbuf or any explicit forwarding signal; only sel_mux = MuxFifo is set. It is unclear from this chunk alone whether full words are correctly forwarded or if data is silently dropped.
uncertain_points.risk: If full message words are not captured, the keccak round receives incomplete data, resulting in incorrect hash or indefinite stall.

uncertain_points.claim: When lc_escalate_en_i forces the FSM to StTerminalError, the block does not assert clr_msgbuf, hold_msg, or any clearing sequence besides sparse_fsm_error_o. The message buffer and keccak round may retain sensitive data (key, message residues) without being wiped.
uncertain_points.cond: Escalation occurs during any active state
uncertain_points.risk: Sensitive data could be recoverable from buffers or pipeline after a fatal error, violating security zeroization policies.

uncertain_points.claim: In StPadFlush, absorbed_d is set to MuBi4True combinatorially upon seeing keccak_complete_i, but the actual absorption acknowledgement (absorbed_o) may appear before the keccak round has fully settled, creating a one-cycle window of premature completion indication.
uncertain_points.risk: External logic acting on absorbed_o too early could read stale or incomplete digest data, though the signal is likely registered downstream.
